content:
We have carbon NMR peaks: 9 signals. Values: 139.25, 134.60, 129.00 (x2), 128.30 (x2), 49.40, 26.10, 11.40.

Methyl carbon typically around 10-15 ppm (for aliphatic CH3). Here we have 11.40 ppm, likely a methyl. Also 26.10 ppm could be a CH2 or CH3 attached to something (maybe isopropyl). 49.40 ppm could be a carbon attached to heteroatom (e.g., CH3 attached to O? Actually O-CH3 ~55 ppm). But we need number of CH3 groups. Methyl carbon signals: each distinct environment gives a peak. 11.40 is definitely a methyl. 26.10 could be a methyl (e.g., isopropyl CH3 ~20 ppm). 49.40 could be a methoxy carbon (O-CH3) ~55 ppm, also methyl. So possibly 3 methyl groups.

But need to confirm using proton NMR maybe. Let's get proton NMR.
